summary: Tested new Super Admin Impersonation feature end-to-end (backend pytest + Playwright UI) plus the two related security fixes and a light MLS/Showcase/Proven-Results regression spot-check. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests passed — POST /api/users/{id}/impersonate returns {access_token, user}, GET /api/auth/me with impersonated token correctly returns target identity (id/name/email) with role forced to 'superuser', _impersonating=true, _impersonator_id, _impersonator_name matching the real admin; self-impersonation returns 400 'You are already this user'; impersonating a nonexistent user returns 404; impersonated token can still call superuser-only GET /api/users (full admin retained); GET /api/users no longer leaks password_hash/password/_id for any user. Frontend: full UI flow verified via Playwright — Impersonate button appears for the other user row ('-' shown for own row), clicking it shows 'Now viewing as <name>' toast, navigates to /dashboard, amber banner appears fixed at top with correct text and Exit button, Topbar correctly shifts down to top-10 (no overlap, verified via bounding box math), banner persists across /contacts, /admin/users, /settings, and Admin Users page remains fully functional while impersonating (verified directly, table renders both user rows + Impersonate buttons). Exit button removes banner, returns to /admin/users, and user menu correctly shows original admin again. Regression spot-check passed: /api/public/listings (Showcase) = 8 active/pending, /api/public/proven-results = 115 sold listings (both match expected counts), and /api/public/listings/{id} for a listing with mls_id set returns 25 already-populated images correctly.

minor.issue: Could not test the 403-for-non-superuser case on POST /users/{id}/impersonate because, per task notes, no non-superuser account currently exists in the system (only 2 duplicate superuser 'Mel' accounts). require_role([SUPERUSER]) dependency is correctly wired (same pattern used by GET /users and other superuser-only routes which do work), so this is very likely fine, but it is unverified against a live non-superuser account.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/utils/auth.py get_current_user() and routes/users.py impersonate_user() correctly handle nested impersonation (attributes to real original admin via _impersonator_id, not the currently-impersonated user) — good defensive design.
Impersonation audit logging to db.impersonation_log is implemented and non-blocking.
AuthContext.impersonate()/exitImpersonation() correctly use a separate 'impersonator_token' localStorage key so the original admin session token is preserved and restored cleanly on exit.
Security fix confirmed: GET /api/users projection now excludes password_hash and password; get_current_user() also strips password/password_hash defensively.
